title: Selective quantization escape: hybrid path adapter to amortize dequant overhead
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: In our mixed-precision serving paths, frequent transitions between quantized (INT8/FP8) kernels and full-precision (FP16/FP32) attention implementations introduce repeated dequant/ requant overheads during prefill and streaming decode. This shows up as per-token tail-latency spikes during short-streamed decodes and wasted GPU cycles in prefill when segments require precision escape.

Goal: Implement a hybrid path adapter — 'Selective Quantization Escape' — that: (1) routes requests through quantized kernels by default, (2) detects precision-sensitive segments at prefill time with a lightweight heuristic, (3) amortizes necessary dequantization work across batch boundaries and the KV cache lifecycle, and (4) selects fused attention kernels that avoid materializing large intermediate dequant buffers (zero-copy or in-place scale-correction) when possible.

Design summary:
- Path adapter component in the runtime that maintains a per-request precision hint and a short-lived escape token window.
- Heuristic: during prefill, compute a single-pass precision score for each layer block using max-abs and softmax-sensitivity estimate; only mark a block for escape if score > threshold. Threshold is dynamically tunable per model profile.
- Amortization strategies: group dequantization work with KV-precompute for the next N tokens, perform lazy requantization at the end of the microbatch, and use a GPU-friendly fused kernel that applies scale-correction without writing an FP32 intermediate when model supports scaled integer attention.
- Kernel selection logic: prefer fused QKV->scaled-attn->context kernels on quantized path; fall back to full-precision fused attention only for marked blocks. Provide hardware-specific implementations: NVIDIA Ampere/Turing kernels vs AMD MI200 kernels selectable at runtime.

Trade-offs and constraints:
- Adds complexity to request routing and kernel selection. Must avoid increasing worst-case tail latency for forced-escape requests.
- Heuristic false-positives may cause unnecessary escapes; false-negatives may cause quality regressions. We must ship with conservative defaults and a per-customer config flag.
- Some models (very large vocabulary or heavy prefix prompts) may not see amortization benefits; monitoring required.

Measuring success: end-to-end decode P50/P95 latency, tokens/sec throughput for prefill workloads, and generation quality (BLEU/ROUGE/QA evals) for a small prompt benchmark. Target: reduce dequant-related per-token overhead by >= 50% on typical streaming workloads and avoid >1% quality regressions on evaluation prompts.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime exposes hybrid path adapter toggle and per-model threshold config
End-to-end streaming decode P95 improves by at least 6% on our 'short-gen' benchmark with default tuning
Prefill throughput improves by at least 8% on quantized models in microbatch sizes 4-16 due to amortized dequant work
No quality regression >1% on the canonical eval prompt set (generation likelihood and task-specific scores) when adapter is enabled with default threshold
Unit and integration tests for kernel selection logic and escape-window behavior added to runtime test suite
Benchmark dashboard updated with before/after comparisons and CI guardrails to detect regressions

comments: 2026-02-18 Maya Chen: Created ticket after spike showed 0.9ms mean dequant/scale overhead per token for short streaming workloads on INT8 path. Linked initial notebook and perf traces: https://confluence.internal.redwood/display/INF/quant-adapter-spike

2026-02-22 Arjun Patel: Implemented initial adapter prototype in branch feature/selective-quant-escape. Baseline microbench shows 35% reduction in explicit dequant kernel time but overall P95 improvement only ~3% due to serialization in prefill stage. GitHub PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1234

2026-02-27 Performance Lab: Added fused scale-correction kernel prototype (cuda) — reduces memory writes by ~60% on Ampere. Benchmark: https://dashboards.redwood/internal/perf/quant-adapter?run=2026-02-27

2026-03-03 Design review (Eng+ML): Agreed to add a conservative default threshold and per-model override. Action: add telemetry and a 'escape reason' tag for every request so we can analyze false-positive escapes. — Notes in design doc: https://confluence.internal.redwood/display/INF/Selective+Quant+Escape

2026-03-06 QA: Early integration tests show one failure case where attention softmax underflow on extreme logits caused a marked escape that degraded quality. Mitigation: clamp softmax pre-scale and re-evaluate heuristic. Assigned to Arjun.

2026-03-10 Arjun Patel: Updated prototype to clamp and add a smoothing window in heuristic; rerun microbench. P95 improvement now 7.2% on short-gen benchmark, throughput up 9% for microbatch=8 on 13B INT8 profile. Scheduling PR review for 2026-03-12.
notes: Implementation must be modular: path adapter and kernel registry are pluggable to allow future quant formats (e.g., group-wise quant, new FP8 variants). Work with infra on rollout policy to avoid exposing experimental heuristics to high-SLA enterprise users. Ensure telemetry labels include model, vm-type, microbatch-size, escape-reason, and kernel-id for postmortem analysis.
